cost.method: List-price estimate from resource lifetimes and NAT byte metrics; excludes discounts and separately billed internet transfer.
assumptions: One auto-allocated NAT IP. VM and boot/local SSD lifetimes conservatively end when instance deletion completes.
Temporary disk lifetime starts at its creation request; NAT lifetime starts at router creation.
Uses observed NAT bytes; unreported final intervals, discounts, and separately billed internet transfer are excluded.

measurement_notes: Creates are sequential with cached template artifacts. No model inference or full Coder turn is timed.
Percentiles use nearest rank: sorted sample 10 for p50 and sample 18 for p90, from twenty samples.
HTTP timing starts before POST and ends after the first successful true command. Default Kind guests used 2 vCPU and 1 GiB.
Native timing includes docker exec and the unchanged node CLI; --autostart --blocking ends at guest readiness. Both native arms used 2 vCPU and 2 GiB, checked through the Firecracker API.
Every completed sample retains actual Firecracker launch arguments. The node CLI also reports its actual boot mode after fallback.
Suspend/wake uses a separate 4 GiB guest and a Python process holding 1 GiB of random bytes in RAM. The same process computes the full SHA-256 before and after a same-host restore.
Wake time includes operation completion, restored-route readiness, and the buffer hash query. Only read-only queries retry.
The runtime template copies and checks the two public runtime executables; full compiler/toolchain parity with the GCE image is untested.

setup_fixes: Raise host inotify instances to 1024 and watches to 1048576 so Kind kube-proxy can keep DNS available.
Wait for suspend/wake operation success rather than accepting a sandbox state change before teardown finishes.
Allow SPACE reserved resolver IPs as well as the GitHub domain; verify the denied HTTPS request with DNS bypassed.
Enable two ready native network slots for the node benchmark; Kind defaults this pool to zero.
